messages:
maya: Quick report — the sample-app onboarding guide uses REDWOOD_API_KEY in the Dockerfile but our CLI and SDKs prefer RW_API_KEY. New hires keep pasting REDWOOD_API_KEY into env and then get intermittent 401s after the org key rotates.
liam: Ugh. Is that because the sample app mounts a .env file into the container and docker-compose is overriding local envs?
sam: Yep. Local dev ends up with both keys set in some cases. SDK priority is currently: process.env.RW_API_KEY > process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY > ~/.redwood/credentials. That mismatch is the root cause.
manika: @maya can you paste the snippet?
maya: Sure — here's the relevant part:```yaml
services:
  web:
    environment:
      - REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}
```
maya: New hires export RW_API_KEY locally, but the compose file uses REDWOOD_API_KEY so the container ends up with the stale one.
liam: Does the SDK refresh behavior make it worse? e.g., it retries on 401 and keeps failing silently?
sam: It retries twice with exponential backoff then surfaces error. But when rotation happens mid-session some integrations suppress the error and continue retrying requests that never succeed.
anika: Possible fixes: (1) normalize env names in sample apps to RW_API_KEY only; (2) add a startup check that compares env var(s) and warns if both present; (3) update SDK to log a single WARN when it sees 401s during startup.
maya: I like 2 + 1. Quick win = change compose to read RW_API_KEY and add a tiny entrypoint check that prints: "WARNING: Both REDWOOD_API_KEY and RW_API_KEY set — using RW_API_KEY. Consider rotating and removing REDWOOD_API_KEY from env. See docs link."
liam: For longer term, SDK change idea: make credential precedence configurable and expose an env var SDK_CRED_PRIORITY="RW,REDWOOD,FILE". That way platform teams can match sample app choices.
sre-bot: Incident note auto: Several support tickets last week flagged 401s caused by stale env var in container image. Ticket IDs: #4521 #4527.
sam: Also proposal to add a small CLI command `rw auth inspect` that prints which credential source will be used in this execution environment. Could be a devtools parity thing (python/node/go).
manika: Agree. UX of `rw auth inspect` would be useful during onboarding sessions. Keep output minimal. Example:```
Source: env(RW_API_KEY)
Value: set (redacted)
Config file: ~/.redwood/credentials — not present
```
maya: I'll open a tiny PR to update the sample app compose + add the entrypoint check. @liam can you sketch a follow-up issue for SDK_CRED_PRIORITY and `rw auth inspect`?
liam: Yup, will add issues for node/python/go SDKs and link the PR.
sanika: :thumbsup: (meant anika)
maya: Thanks everyone — hopefully this cuts down onboarding tickets. I'll ping the support channel when PR is up.
